question: Which wife chosen at a well am I?
reference: Genesis 24; 27 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Rebekah')

clues: A servant prayed for a sign: the right woman would offer water to him and to his camels.
I drew water again and again until all ten camels had finished drinking.
I agreed to leave my family that very day to marry a man I had never met.
Years later I helped my favorite son disguise himself to steal his brother's blessing.

question: Which unloved wife am I?
reference: Genesis 29-30 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Leah')

clues: My father married me off by disguising me under a heavy veil.
The Bible notes that my eyes were weak, while my younger sister was beautiful.
I bore six of Jacob's sons and a daughter, hoping each birth would win my husband's love.
From my sons came both the royal tribe and the priestly tribe.

question: Which stubborn king am I?
reference: Exodus 1-14 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Pharaoh')

clues: A new ruler who did not know Joseph turned his people into slaves.
I ordered every Hebrew baby boy to be thrown into the river.
Ten devastating plagues struck my land before I finally let the people go.
I chased them to the edge of the sea with my chariots and was swallowed up.

question: Which father-in-law am I?
reference: Exodus 2; 3; 18 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Jethro')

clues: I was a priest in the land of Midian.
My daughters were driving off shepherds from a well when a fugitive from Egypt stepped in to help them.
I gave him my daughter Zipporah, and he tended my flocks for forty years.
I advised him to stop judging every case himself and to appoint capable men over thousands, hundreds, and tens.

question: Which first judge am I?
reference: Judges 1:12-13; 3:7-11 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Othniel')

clues: I was a younger kinsman of Caleb.
I captured a town called Kiriath-sepher and won Caleb's daughter Achsah as my wife.
When Israel had served a Mesopotamian king for eight years, God's spirit came upon me.
I freed the nation, and the land had rest for forty years.

question: Which cousin of a king am I?
reference: 1 Samuel 14:50; 2 Samuel 2-3 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Abner')

clues: I was the chief of King Saul's army and a relative of his.
After Saul died, I set his son Ish-bosheth on the throne of the northern tribes.
When Ish-bosheth accused me over one of Saul's concubines, I switched my loyalty to David.
Joab took me aside at the gate of Hebron and killed me to avenge his brother.

question: Which foolish landowner am I?
reference: 1 Samuel 25 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Nabal')

clues: I was a very rich man with thousands of sheep and goats near Carmel of Judah.
David's men had guarded my shepherds, but I insulted them and sent them away empty-handed.
My wife rode out with food and kept David from killing every male in my household.
When she told me the next morning, my heart went numb, and about ten days later I died.

question: Which man who touched the ark am I?
reference: 2 Samuel 6:1-11 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Uzzah No. 1')

clues: The ark was being moved on a new wagon rather than carried on poles as the Law required.
The cattle nearly upset it at a threshing floor.
I reached out my hand to steady the sacred chest.
God struck me down on the spot, and the frightened king left the ark at a nearby house for three months.

question: Which first king of the northern kingdom am I?
reference: 1 Kings 11-12 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Jeroboam No. 1')

clues: I began as an officer over Solomon's forced-labor gangs.
A prophet tore his new garment into twelve pieces and handed me ten of them.
After Solomon's son threatened to make the people's load heavier, ten tribes made me their king.
I set up golden calves at Bethel and Dan so my subjects would not travel to Jerusalem to worship.

question: Which vineyard owner am I?
reference: 1 Kings 21 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Naboth')

clues: My land lay right next to the palace of the king in Jezreel.
He offered to buy it or trade for it, but it was my ancestral inheritance and I would not give it up.
His queen hired scoundrels to testify that I had cursed God and the king.
I was dragged out and stoned, and the king went down to take possession of my vineyard.

question: Which lone true prophet am I?
reference: 1 Kings 22 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Micaiah No. 2')

clues: Two kings sat on their thrones while 400 prophets promised them victory.
I was summoned last, and at first I sarcastically told the king to go up and win.
Then I said what I had really seen: Israel scattered on the mountains like sheep without a shepherd.
The king jailed me on bread and water until he should return in peace, but he never came back.

question: Which prophetess am I?
reference: 2 Kings 22:14-20 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Huldah')

clues: I lived in Jerusalem in the days of a boy-king who grew into a great reformer.
When the lost book of the Law was found in the temple, the king sent his officials to me.
I confirmed that the curses written in the book would come upon the nation.
But I promised the faithful king that he would be gathered to his grave in peace, not seeing the calamity.

question: Which palace official am I?
reference: Esther 2-10 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Mordecai No. 2')

clues: I raised my orphaned younger cousin as if she were my own daughter.
I overheard two doorkeepers plotting to assassinate the king and reported it.
I refused to bow to the king's proud favorite, who then schemed to destroy my whole people.
In the end I was led through the city in royal robes, and later I received the signet ring of the man who had hated me.

question: Which elderly priest am I?
reference: Luke 1:5-25, 57-79 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Zechariah No. 16')

clues: I was serving in the temple when an angel appeared beside the altar of incense.
The angel promised that my wife Elizabeth would bear a son in our old age.
Because I doubted, I could not speak until the child was born.
When I wrote that his name would be John, my tongue was freed and I prophesied.

question: Which king who feared a rival am I?
reference: Matthew 2 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Herod No. 1')

clues: Astrologers came to my court asking where the king of the Jews had been born.
I quietly asked them to bring me word once they had found the child.
When they went home another way, I ordered the killing of all the boys in Bethlehem two years old and under.
But the child had already been taken to Egypt out of my reach.

question: Which blind beggar am I?
reference: Mark 10:46-52 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Bartimaeus')

clues: I sat begging beside the road as people streamed out of Jericho.
Hearing that Jesus was passing, I called out, "Son of David, have mercy on me!"
The crowd told me to be quiet, so I shouted all the louder.
Jesus called me over, my sight came back, and I followed him on the road.
